reason: Start gathering the giant's dusty disk material with stones toward its moons.
expectation: The stones and disk material may form a rocky moon or an intermediate aggregate.

alternatives.reason: The ice-rich material also fits a goal, but I chose to follow the dusty disk first.

effect: The dusty disk produced rocky moonlets, which can now gather further material.
reaction: The moonlets are a satisfying first step toward the giant's moons.
reason: Follow the separate ice-rich material while it is available.
expectation: The ice-rich pieces may gather into icy moonlets or another fragile aggregate.

alternatives.reason: Adding dust could grow the rocky moonlets, but I want to start the ice-rich path first.

effect: The ice-rich material formed separate moonlets, opening several possible encounters.
reaction: I'm curious how fragile these moonlets are when struck.
reason: Follow the fragile ice-rich material through a fast impact, directly addressing the second goal.
expectation: The fast stones may break the ice-rich moonlets into fragments.

alternatives.reason: Adding icy fragments might grow the moonlets, but the impact seems more relevant to their fragility.

effect: The impact broke one small icy moon and completed the fragile-material goal; the moon-making goal remains.
reaction: The destructive outcome matched my expectation and clarified that the other moonlets remain.
reason: Add dust to the rocky moonlets to pursue the remaining moon-building goal.
expectation: The moonlets may gather dust and grow into a larger rocky moon or an intermediate body.

alternatives.reason: Growing the icy moonlets also seems relevant, but I chose to continue the rocky path first.

effect: The rocky moonlet grew into a moon, but the moon-building goal remains incomplete.
reaction: It's satisfying to see a moon form, though it evidently isn't the whole goal.
reason: Grow the ice-rich moonlets as well to pursue the remaining goal.
expectation: The icy fragments may help one moonlet grow into an ice-rich moon.

alternatives.reason: The rocky moon could encounter fast stones, but growing another moon seems more directly relevant.

effect: An ice-rich moon formed, but the moon-building goal remains open.
reaction: The second moon formed as expected; I'm curious what remains to complete the goal.
reason: Test how fast stones affect the larger rocky moon, contrasting it with the shattered icy moonlet.
expectation: The rocky moon may retain its shape but acquire craters; I'm unsure whether that advances the goal.

alternatives.reason: The ice-rich moon could also be struck, but the rocky moon offers a contrast to the earlier icy impact.

effect: The rocky moon survived the impacts with fresh craters, completing the remaining goal and the chapter.
reaction: The contrast with the shattered smaller icy moon was satisfying, though the result matched my expectation.

mostWorthwhile.text: Striking the rocky moon was worthwhile because it contrasted a cratered survivor with the earlier broken moonlet.

leastWorthwhile.text: Growing the two types of moonlets felt somewhat repetitive, although it established their different materials.

surprise.text: Making both a rocky and an ice-rich moon did not complete the moon-building goal; the rocky moon's impact did.

arbitrary.text: The need to crater the rocky moon to complete a goal about making moons was not clear beforehand.

continue.text: I would continue for another chapter to see how the surviving moons and fragments develop, though the repeated growth steps temper my interest.
